title: daily-scratchpad-gpu-ops-08
content:
Daily scratchpad - GPU ops / infra (quick notes, todo, commands)

2026-02-28 quick log before EOD:
- Spin up extra p4d pool for batch-run A/B test (target 8 nodes) -> blocked by quota in us-west2. Raised request to cloud-quotas (case #).
- Noted high tail latency on small-reqs between 09:30-10:15; suspect noisy neighbor on node set gpuc-uw2-a.

Things to follow up (priority order):
1) Quota bump for us-west2 GPUs (p4d) - needed for canary burst on 2026-03-05. Contact: cloud-quotas@ and CC finance (cost approval pending).
2) Investigate noisy neighbor: capture cpu/gpu metrics on gpuc-uw2-a nodes, check process list, docker stats.
3) Network MTU mismatch on subnet infra-vpc-2 causing intermittent drops for 10-15% of pods (seen with large model KV sync). Quick test: run iperf between nodes, check host routing tables.
4) Confirm autoscaler policy for dedicated pools: make sure maxSurge and buffer settings applied after deploy. PR staging -> prod rollout still scheduled.

Commands / snippets I used / keep handy:
- kubectl top nodes --selector=gpu=true --sort-by=cpu
- nvidia-smi dmon -s u -d 5 (run for 2 minutes to check utilization spikes)
- sudo tc qdisc show dev eth0  # quick mtu/queue diagnostics
- gcloud compute regions describe us-west2 --project=redwood-inference-project

Notes from meeting w/ Samir (2026-03-02):
- Capacity plan v2: aim for 20% headroom during peak (09:00-11:00) for prod-hosted; Dedicated customers reserve separately.
- Need clearer alert thresholds: gpu_util > 88% for > 5m -> page on-call. Current rule uses 95% which is too late.
- Action: update alerting playbook + runbook for pgpu-ops.

Open tasks (short):
- [ ] Update alert thresholds in prometheus for gpu-util (Samir) - target change by 2026-03-04
- [ ] Submit quota request follow-up (Alex) - include cost estimate and timeline
- [ ] Run iperf between gpuc-uw2-a and gpuc-uw2-b and paste results in ticket JIRA-3245 (Jamie)
- [ ] Validate autoscaler config after next deploy (Alex/Jamie)
- [ ] Add example troubleshooting section to runbook: "KV cache warmup fail" (small checklist + commands)

Quick troubleshooting checklist (first-pass):
- check node allocations: kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node>
- check GPU processes: docker exec -it <container> bash && ps aux | grep python / jupyter
- check kernel logs for oom/killed processes: journalctl -u kubelet -n 200
- test network: sudo ethtool -k eth0; iperf3 -c <peer> -P 4 -t 30

Random notes / hypotheses:
- Might be worth testing smaller CPU requests on replica controller for transformer-serve to reduce noisy neighbor effects (reduce OOM events).
- Consider pinning critical routes to dedicated pool when latency-sensitive (hosted-api low-latency class).

Reference tickets / links:
- JIRA-3245: "Investigate tail latency and noisy neighbor on us-west2 gpuc nodes"
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/482 (autoscaler tweak + docs)
- Confluence: Runtime Capacity Plan v2 (link saved in linked_artifacts)

Meeting notes to keep (short):
- 2026-03-03 sync: confirm quota status, Samir to escalate with cloud vendor contact if no response by EOB 2026-03-04.
- Next steps: run targeted repro at 09:30-10:00 to capture spike, attach profiles to JIRA ticket.

Notes to self: keep this doc lightweight, move stable procedures to runbook/Confluence once validated.

-- Alex
